newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian April inflationary expectations steady.
newsitem.headline: Australian April inflationary expectations steady.

text.p: The inflationary expectations of Australian consumers for the coming year were unchanged in April, the Melbourne Institute said on Thursday.
The median April consumer expectation was for a 3.5 percent rise in inflation over the next 12 months, the same response given for March 1997.

"It is encouraging to note that in the six months from November 1996 to April 1997, median expectations of inflation fluctuated between a low of 3.4 percent and a high of 3.7 percent," the institute said.
It said this compared favourably with the seven months from April 1996 to October 1996 in which expectations fluctuated between four and 4.5 percent.
"This suggests that median inflation expectations have fallen by between 0.6 and 0.8 percent over the past year," the institute said.

"While such revisions to expectations might seem stubbornly slow, it is encouraging to note that if this rate of decline in inflationary expectations continues over the coming year, then the median consumer's expectation of inflation will lie within the Reserve Bank's target range of two to three percent."
"Given that actual (December quarter) inflation was 1.5 percent such a further decline in expectations is quite plausible," it said.
The institute said the possibility of such a further decline in expectations was increased by its finding that consumer's median notion of inflation now was 2.5 percent in April 1997.

"If as anticipated, inflationary expectations over the coming year decline to lie within the Reserve Bank's target range then, that outcome would be a further achievement for monetary policy, especially when viewed against Australia's past inflation performance," it said.
March quarter consumer price index figures are due to be released next Wednesday.
